The *Sattakauddesa* (Pp 1.7) is a section of the *Puggalapaññatti*, a canonical treatise belonging to the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It serves as the uddesa (table of contents or matrix of headings) listing categories of persons grouped into sets of seven [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records one translation of the text across one language [SuttaCentral].

DharmaNexus identifies 26 instances of internal Pali text reuse between the *Sattakauddesa* and four other canonical and post-canonical Pali works [DharmaNexus]. Within the *Puggalapaññatti* itself, it exhibits extensive reuse with the corresponding expository section, the *Sattakapuggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.7), which elaborates upon the classifications outlined in this uddesa [DharmaNexus]. In the Sutta Piṭaka, it shares significant parallel phrasing with the *Sattakanipāta* of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 7), with ten matching passages [DharmaNexus]. Additional textual matches are identified with the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi* (Tika Abh09t) and the *Vimokkhakathā* of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 1.5) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus records no cross-language matches with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora meeting the score threshold [DharmaNexus].
